title: Whose Data, Whose Benchmark? A User-Centric Framework for Auditing Evaluation Resources
abstract: arXiv:2610.19268v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Benchmarks shape how model capabilities are measured and interpreted, yet their scores can obscure whose conventions, contexts, and judgments define successful performance. We introduce a user-centric audit framework that distinguishes users who contribute benchmark content from those whose needs evaluation results are intended to represent. The framework operationalizes seven dimensions across benchmark content, metadata, documentation, and scoring procedures. Across 16 resources, we find that American-centered conventions account for 62.4-94.4% of matched signals in 11 text benchmarks, while geographic visibility in five image-text resources is concentrated and strongly associated with national GDP share (mean Pearson r = 0.780; Spearman p = 0.778). translated_title: 谁的数据，谁的基准？一个用于审计评估资源的以用户为中心的框架
translated_abstract: 基准测试塑造了模型能力被衡量和解读的方式，然而其分数可能掩盖了“是谁的惯例、情境和判断定义了成功的表现”。我们提出了一个以用户为中心的审计框架，该框架区分了贡献基准内容的用户与评估结果旨在代表的用户。该框架在基准内容、元数据、文档和评分程序四个方面具体化了七个维度。通过对16个资源的分析，我们发现：在11个文本基准中，以美国为中心的惯例占据了62.4%至94.4%的匹配信号；而在五个图文资源中，地理可见性高度集中，并与国家GDP份额呈强相关（平均Pearson r = 0.780；Spearman ρ = 0.778）。文档分析揭示了一个系统性的“来源-目标”差距：所有16个资源都具体化了来源用户情境，但没有任何一个具体化了目标用户情境。配对评分实验进一步表明……
tldr: 该论文提出了一个以用户为中心的基准测试审计框架，通过七个维度对评估资源进行审计，揭示了现有基准中美国中心惯例占主导地位、地理可见性与GDP强相关、以及来源用户情境被纳入而目标用户情境完全缺失的系统性偏差。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces a user-centric audit framework for evaluation benchmarks, revealing that existing resources are dominated by American-centric conventions (62.4-94.4% of matched signals), show GDP-correlated geographic visibility, and systematically include source-user contexts while entirely lacking target-user contexts.
